# State-dependent EB-event renewal has an ordering obstruction
2026-10-29. Exact rejected extension.

It is tempting to replace a constant-weight EB CPTP branch by an EB trace-nonincreasing event E≤CPΨ with E†I≥αI. Let R=Ψ−E. Then ||R||diamond≤1−α and the left-resolvent sum Fleft=ΣR^n E has the desired identity id−Fleft=(id−R)^−1(id−Ψ). But Fleft need not be TP.

Counterexample: classical2-state channels in column convention,
E=[[1/2,3/4],[0,0]], R=[[0,0],[1/2,1/4]].
Their sum Ψ is stochastic. E is an EB event with input effect diag(1/2,3/4)≥I/2. Nevertheless
Fleft=(I−R)^−1E=[[1/2,3/4],[1/3,1/2]],
whose column sums are5/6 and5/4. It is not TP and is trace-increasing on the second input.

The physical first-hit channel Fright=ΣE R^n=E(I−R)^−1=[[1,1],[0,0]] IS TP by effect telescoping. But its identity has the other ordering,
id−Fright=(id−Ψ)(id−R)^−1,
which does not directly bound its disturbance by the original one-step residual. Additional commutation or structural control would be required. The constant-weight CPTP theorem avoids the issue because every term has a state-independent scalar trace weight.

Thus full-rank event effects alone do not establish the proposed left-resolvent EB-channel claim. This does not rule out a different instrument-based construction.

# Safe finite-depth salvage for state-dependent EB events
2026-10-29. Root-derived replacement for the rejected left-renewal claim; independent review pending.

Let Ψ be CPTP and Ψ=E+R, where E is CP entanglement-breaking (not necessarily TP), R is CP, and E†I≥αI, α>0. Then R†I≤(1−α)I, so ||R^m||diamond≤(1−α)^m.

The noncommutative expansion Ψ^m−R^m is a sum of CP words containing E, hence is CP and entanglement-breaking. Its trace deficit is the positive effect (R^m)†I. Fix a density operator τ and complete it by the EB replacement event
B_m(X)=(Ψ^m−R^m)(X)+Tr[R^m(X)]τ.
This is CPTP and EB, with halfdiamond distance from Ψ^m at most(1−α)^m: the difference is R^m minus its replacement completion, each term having diamond norm at most(1−α)^m.

For any state with arbitrary reference, telescoping and CPTP trace contraction give
T(ρ,Ψ^mρ)≤Σ_(k=0)^(m−1)T(Ψ^kρ,Ψ^(k+1)ρ)≤m T(ρ,Ψρ).
Therefore
T(ρ,B_mρ)≤m T(ρ,Ψρ)+(1−α)^m.
If Ψ is the actual universal recovered channel, averaging yields
**e_avg(B_m)≤m√δ+(1−α)^m.**
Choosing m of order log(1/δ)/α yields a square-root-loss times logarithmic factor, not the constant√δ bound of the state-independent branch theorem. The reference version retains the product-barycenter assumption needed for recovery factorization, and the comparator is EB on the noisy system only.

This construction neither normalizes the invalid left-resolvent nor assumes its trace preservation. It is a separate valid finite-depth channel construction. Existence/acquisition of a suitable event E with a uniform full-rank effect remains an additional obligation for any proposed channel family. No cheap physical implementation or novelty claim is asserted.

2026-10-29. Additive clarification; original governing file unchanged.

For the generic EB-mixture theorem, if ν=Φσ is rank deficient, let P=suppν. The primary recovery is TP on P. Extend it to the entire output algebra by R_ext(Y)=R(PYP)+Tr[(I−P)Y]σ. This is CPTP, agrees with recovery on all relevant outputs, and fixes the prior through R_extΦσ=σ. Use this extended recovery before calling R_extB and R_extC channels. For faithfulσ, every Φρ is supported in P. In particular every actual ensemble letter is covered. In the unital-qubit case, faithfulσ implies faithfulΦσ directly.

The general governing proof is stated for faithfulσ. To justify the unital-qubit conclusion for EVERY prior: a singular qubit prior is rank one, so every positive-weight ensemble letter equals that pure state. Constant re-preparation has zero error. In the product-reference version with meanσ_A⊗ω_R and rank-oneσ_A, positivity forces every letter to factor as σ_A⊗ρ_R,x; replacement on A again has zero disturbance. No singular Petz inverse is needed for this case.
